116,283 km2 for 1111-1187, the same area as the 1202 shape. 'It became an independent principality in 1125' under Rostislav Mstislavich (1125-1160, Rostislav page); the shape is held from 1111 as Cliopatria has it. The Vitebsk page has Smolensk's princes acquiring Vitebsk in 1165-1167 and again influencing it from 1186: contests, not a change of shape.

The Vitebsk page has only Vitebsk, not Polotsk, 'fell under the influence of Smolensk' in 1186 and the princes who 'in 1195 marched against the prince of Smolensk' restored Vitebsk to Polotsk's rule. That is a contest (ledger 1186-1195), not annexation, so the shape is the 1111 shape.

116,283 km2 (1202-1240), the 1111 shape. The page has Mstislav Romanovich and Vladimir Riurikovich on the Kievan throne 1212-1235, the Lithuanians holding Smolensk briefly in 1239 and Yaroslav Vsevolodovich expelling them the next year. No frontier moves.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Smolensk shape for 1241-1293 (its Mongol Empire shape from 1241 covers 520 of the 522 cells of the 1202 shape). The pages keep the principality alive: 'Although spared by the Mongol armies in 1240, Smolensk paid tribute to the Golden Horde' (Smolensk page), Mindaugas's troops 'repeatedly devastate the principality' in the mid-13th century and 'by the late 13th century' it was 'dependent on the Grand Principality of Vladimir' (principality page). No page gives its extent: the 1202 shape is assumed, confidence 1. The Horde's tribute is a vassal relation for the golden-horde or mongol-empire dossier to carry.

150,993 km2 for 1294-1304: the 1202 shape plus 153 cells (about 34,700 km2, Gomel in the south-west and Rzhev in the north-east; Mozhaysk is already inside the 1202 shape). No page opened dates or describes that growth; the principality page says only that Smolensk was dependent on Vladimir in the late 13th century. The Velikiye Luki page puts Luki in the Novgorod Republic 'from the 12th century', and Cliopatria's Smolensk shape (1294-1374) holds Luki and Toropets, an unresolved conflict. Unverified: page budget.

region.text: Smolensk and its land as Cliopatria draws the 1056 shape

ledger.note: 1054: Smolensk becomes the share of Vyacheslav Yaroslavich, the first of Yaroslav's descendants to rule it. 'Vyacheslav Yaroslavich begins the rule of Yaroslav I's descendants, who governed until 1125'; the city page: 'The Principality of Smolensk was founded in 1054'. The land is the 1056 shape; the pages give no boundary.

1125: Rostislav Mstislavich becomes prince of Smolensk and the principality is independent. 'It became an independent principality in 1125' (infobox 'Established: 1125'); the Rostislav page: 'Prince of Smolensk (1125-1160)', with his sons Roman, Mstislav and Davyd after him (Rurik held Belgorod). A new line on the same land.

1165: the princes of Smolensk take Vitebsk from Polotsk's line. 'In 1165-1167 due to the feudal strife, the principality of Vitebsk was shortly acquired by the princes of Smolensk' ('Smolensk rule (1167-1168)' in the princes' list).
1168: Briachislav Vasilkovich recovers Vitebsk ('Briachislav Vasilkovich (1168-1175)'; 'Vitebsk later regained independence').

1186: Vitebsk again falls under Smolensk's influence, which angered Polotsk and Chernigov: 'In 1186, the principality of Vitebsk again fell under the influence of Smolensk.' Cliopatria draws the whole Polotsk-Vitebsk core as Smolensk from 1188; the page names only Vitebsk.
1195: the Polotsk and Chernigov princes who 'in 1195 marched against the prince of Smolensk' restore Vitebsk to Polotsk's rule.
1239: the Lithuanians briefly capture Smolensk: '1239: Lithuanians briefly capture Smolensk. Yaroslav Vsevolodovich expels them the following year.'

1240: Yaroslav Vsevolodovich expels the Lithuanians from Smolensk, which the Mongols spare: 'Although spared by the Mongol armies in 1240, Smolensk paid tribute to the Golden Horde' (city page). Cliopatria ends its first Smolensk row here and covers the land with the Mongol Empire from 1241.

region.text: Smolensk and Rzhev, taken by Algirdas and contested with Moscow in 1356-1359

ledger.note: 1356: Algirdas captures Smolensk and Bryansk ('In 1356, Algirdas captured Bryansk and Smolensk'); the Algirdas page says he 'occupied Smolensk and Bryansk' without a date. Simeon of Moscow had entered Smolensk in 1352 and removed the pro-Lithuanian prince.

1359: Algirdas regains Smolensk and Rzhev and takes Mstislavl, after Ivan II's 1358 expedition had driven the Lithuanians out of Rzhev ('In 1358 ... drives Lithuanians out of Rzhev'; 'In 1359, Algirdas regains Smolensk and Rzhev and takes Mstislavl'). Smolensk keeps its own prince under Lithuanian influence: it joins a campaign against Moscow in 1368 and fights beside Moscow in 1372-1374.

wars.name: Smolensk's claims on Vitebsk
wars.outcome: Smolensk's princes held Vitebsk in 1165-1168 and again had influence over it from 1186; the Polotsk and Chernigov princes marched against the prince of Smolensk in 1195 and restored Vitebsk to Polotsk's rule.
wars.note: Two episodes, 1165-1168 and 1186-1195; mirrored in the principality-of-polotsky dossier.

wars.name: Treaty of Smolensk with Riga over Polotsk
wars.outcome: 'In 1227 Smolensk ceded Polotsk by treaty to the city of Riga'; the Polotsk page adds that 'For short periods, the neighbouring Principality of Smolensk also claimed control over some lands of the principality'.
wars.note: Smolensk's shape never contains Polotsk after 1201 in Cliopatria, so no border moves; the claim is recorded here, the vassalage to the Livonian Brothers (1227-1240) in the other dossiers.

wars.name: Mongol invasion (Smolensk spared)
wars.outcome: Smolensk escaped destruction in 1238-1240 ('Although spared by the Mongol armies in 1240, Smolensk paid tribute to the Golden Horde'); Cliopatria's Mongol Empire shape nevertheless covers its land from 1241.
wars.note: The Mongol invasion page says Smolensk escaped destruction or suffered little, without dates.

wars.name: Golden Horde order against Ivan Aleksandrovich of Smolensk
wars.outcome: 'Ozbeg Khan orders Russian princes to campaign against Ivan Aleksandrovich over unpaid tribute'; the page gives no result.

wars.name: Moscow and Lithuania for Smolensk
wars.outcome: Simeon of Moscow entered Smolensk in 1352 and removed the pro-Lithuanian prince; Algirdas captured Bryansk and Smolensk in 1356; a Muscovite expedition drove the Lithuanians from Rzhev in 1358; Algirdas regained Smolensk and Rzhev and took Mstislavl in 1359.
wars.note: The Principality of Moscow page gives the same years (1352, 1356, 1358, 1359).

wars.name: Vytautas's conquest of Smolensk
wars.outcome: Vytautas captured Smolensk in 1395 and Vasily I accepted the annexation in 1396; Smolensk revolted in 1401 and recalled Yury; Vytautas reasserted control in 1404 and the principality became the 'Smolensk land' of Lithuania.
wars.note: The Vytautas page has the Vorskla defeat of 1399 and George of Smolensk retaking the city before 1404; the city page adds a capture in 1408.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages opened; the frontiers with Polotsk, Chernigov, Novgorod, Moscow and Lithuania are approximate throughout.

notes: Pages opened: Principality of Smolensk, Smolensk (city), Algirdas, Vytautas, Principality of Moscow, Rostislav Mstislavich, Velikiye Luki (own budget 9: 7 used) plus Principality of Vitebsk, Principality of Polotsk and the Mongol invasion page shared with the Polotsk, Rostov-Suzdal and Ryazan dossiers. Start 1054 follows the principality and city pages; end 1404 follows the principality page (Cliopatria to 1406). Cliopatria's Mongol Empire shape covers 520 of 522 cells of the 1202 shape from 1241 to 1293: the new 1241-1293 keyframe is the 1202 shape (confidence 1) so the state has no hole; the Horde's tribute is a vassal relation (mongol-empire or golden-horde dossier, counterpart principality-of-smolensk). Cliopatria faults: (1) 1188-1201 adds the Polotsk-Vitebsk core, which the Vitebsk page makes only a contest over Vitebsk in 1186-1195; (2) the shape holds Mozhaysk until 1406 though Moscow seized it in 1304; the 60 km disc is mine (no Mozhaysk in the gazetteer: name needed, place, 55.51N 36.03E); (3) the 1294-1374 shapes hold Velikiye Luki and Toropets, which the Velikiye Luki page makes Novgorod's; (4) the 1363 and 1375 losses are Cliopatria's and fall in Lithuania's shape. Not on any page opened: the 1294 growth, the 1314 redraw, the 1363 and 1375 losses' causes and dates, Smolensk's extent in 1241-1293, the 1396-1400 status. The city page has Vytautas taking Smolensk in 1408, against the principality page's 1404; the Vytautas page puts the retaking by George after 1399. In 1173 two Smolensk princes captured Kiev (Vsevolod the Big Nest page) and 1212-1235 Smolensk princes held the Kievan throne: no territory.
